science_brief: Science brief: earth and space processes span timescales from seconds to billions of years and spatial scales from grains to galaxies.
Science brief: a process observable at one scale may be invisible at another, so the scale of observation determines what can be concluded.
Science brief: slow processes accumulate large effects over long times, which is why geologic change is substantial despite being imperceptible year to year.
Science brief: extrapolating a rate measured over a short interval to a much longer one requires evidence that the rate is constant.

disqualifying_errors: Inferring causation from correlation alone.
Rejecting a well-supported causal claim on the grounds that the evidence is correlational, when mechanism and multiple lines of evidence are present.
Asserting a mechanism with no evidence and treating that as having established causation.
fixed_facts: Correlation between two variables does not establish that one causes the other.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Formal causal inference frameworks are beyond this course.
relationships: Two variables can correlate because one causes the other, because a third factor drives both, or by coincidence in a limited sample.
Establishing causation requires a mechanism, evidence that cause precedes effect, and where possible a controlled comparison.
In Earth science, controlled experiments are often impossible, so causal claims rest on mechanism plus multiple independent lines of evidence.

disqualifying_errors: Treating a proxy measurement as a direct measurement of the quantity it stands for.
Reporting a proxy reconstruction with no reference to its calibration or uncertainty.
Basing a reconstruction on one proxy and presenting it as settled.
fixed_facts: A proxy is a measurable quantity that stands in for a quantity that cannot be measured directly, and it requires a calibrated relationship between the two.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Specific proxy calibration methodology and age-model construction are beyond this course.
relationships: Ice cores, tree rings, sediment layers, corals, and isotope ratios are proxies for past conditions.
A proxy carries the uncertainty of the calibration as well as of the measurement itself.
Independent proxies agreeing is what makes a reconstruction robust; a single proxy carries much weaker support.

science_brief: Science brief: hydrogen and helium formed in the early universe; elements up to iron are produced by fusion in stars; most elements heavier than iron are produced by neutron capture in evolved stars and in explosive events.
Science brief: fusion releases energy up to iron, and beyond iron fusion consumes rather than releases energy, which is why stellar fusion does not build the heaviest elements.
Science brief: heavier elements are dispersed into space by stellar winds and supernovae, enriching the material from which later stars and planets form.
Science brief: the atoms in Earth and in living things were produced in earlier generations of stars.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Looking at the sun causes permanent eye damage.
MITIGATION: NEVER look at the sun directly, through any lens, grating, CD, camera, or filter. All solar work is done by measuring warming water in shade-versus-sun, with the learner's back to the sun.
HAZARD (physical): Working outdoors in sun risks heat and sunburn, and a sealed dark container left in full sun pressurises.
MITIGATION: Leave the water container OPEN - never capped or sealed - in the sun. Limit exposure to 30 minutes at a time, wear a hat and sunscreen, keep drinking water available, and work in the cooler part of the day.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be beside you, watching, for the whole investigation. Do not start any step until they are there.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. The published-data route is the DEFAULT and needs no outdoor work at all.
  SAFE ORDER 2. If the outdoor route runs, the learner works with their back to the sun and never looks toward it - not directly and not through a lens, filter, grating, CD, or camera.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Wear a hat and sunscreen, take drinking water, and work in the cooler part of the day, for no more than 30 minutes at a time.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Leave the dark water container OPEN in the sun; it is never capped or sealed.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Read the thermometer at fixed intervals from the shade, and come indoors at the scheduled end or at the first sign of overheating.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop instantly if anyone looks toward the sun through any optical device.
  STOP: Stop and move indoors at any sign of overheating.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pour the water down the drain and dry the container, and return the CD or grating to its sleeve. Nothing hazardous is produced, and no image of the sun is captured by any means.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Skip all outdoor solar work: compute the sun's power output and lifetime from published solar-constant and mass data, and identify elements from published stellar spectra images. Paper and calculator only. This is the DEFAULT path.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

Science brief: the atoms in Earth and in living things were produced in earlier generations of stars.

science_brief: Science brief: each element produces a characteristic pattern of spectral lines, which is how the composition of distant objects is determined.
Science brief: emission lines appear where atoms release specific energies; absorption lines appear where atoms remove those same energies from light passing through.
Science brief: because the line pattern is characteristic of the element, a spectrum identifies which elements are present without any sample being collected.
Science brief: line positions also carry information about motion, through Doppler shift, and about conditions such as temperature and pressure.

Asteroids, comets, and Kuiper belt objects are remnants of that formation process and carry evidence about it.

READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Pins used to draw ellipses can prick or be stepped on.
MITIGATION: Push pins into a cardboard backing on a table, count them out and back in, and keep them away from young children and off the floor.

  SAFE ORDER 2. Count the pins out and record the number before starting.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Draw the ellipses with the pins staying in the cardboard the whole time.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Count every pin back in and account for all of them before anyone leaves the work area.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop and account for every pin before leaving the work area.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.

  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Pins go back into a closed labelled container, counted, and stored out of reach of young children. Recycle the cardboard. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Construct ellipses with a compass and ruler rather than pins and string, and complete all orbital prediction arithmetically from the published dataset. Paper only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming the plates float on a layer of liquid magma.
Claiming Earth's internal heat comes principally from the Sun.
Claiming the entire outer core and mantle are molten; only the outer core is liquid.
fixed_facts: Earth's mantle is solid rock that deforms and flows very slowly; it is not a liquid layer.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Mantle rheology and geodynamic modelling are beyond this course.
relationships: Heat from Earth's interior, from residual formation heat and radioactive decay, drives slow convective flow in the mantle.
Mantle flow, together with the pull of dense subducting slabs and the push at ridges, drives plate motion.
The mantle behaves as a solid on short timescales and flows on geological ones, which is why seismic shear waves pass through it.

science_brief: Science brief: oceanic crust is denser and thinner than continental crust, which is why oceanic crust subducts beneath continental crust.
Science brief: oceanic crust forms at spreading ridges from mantle-derived magma and is returned to the mantle at subduction zones.
Science brief: continental crust is less dense, so it resists subduction and can survive for billions of years.
Science brief: subduction generates magma that rises to build volcanic arcs and adds to continental crust over time.

science_brief: Science brief: groundwater occupies pore spaces and fractures in rock and sediment; it does not generally flow in open underground rivers.
Science brief: surface water and groundwater are connected: streams gain from or lose to groundwater depending on the water table.
Science brief: groundwater moves far more slowly than surface water, so contamination is slow to appear and slow to clear.
Science brief: extraction faster than recharge lowers the water table and can cause land subsidence and saltwater intrusion.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): Soil and outdoor materials carry bacteria and sharp fragments.
MITIGATION: Cover any cut or graze with a waterproof dressing before handling soil, wear gloves, keep hands away from the face, wash thoroughly afterwards, and never use soil from an area treated with pesticide or near a roadway.
HAZARD (physical): Soil on kitchen equipment contaminates everything used with it afterwards.
MITIGATION: The trays, cups, and measuring container are labelled for this investigation and never return to food use. Nothing from this investigation is washed in a kitchen sink.
HAZARD (physical): Water and soil together make surfaces slippery, and soil runoff blocks indoor drain traps.
MITIGATION: Work outdoors or over a large tray, clean spills immediately, and pour all runoff outdoors onto ground or through a strainer into an outdoor drain - never down a kitchen or bathroom sink.
HAZARD (privacy): Photographing or logging a field site can reveal where the family lives.
MITIGATION: Record substrate type, slope, and conditions only. No address, GPS coordinate, or identifiable landmark is recorded, and no photograph is required.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. Use only the trays, cups, and measuring container labelled for this investigation. None of them has been used for food and none returns to food use.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Confirm the soil source with the adult: never soil from a treated area, a roadside, or an unknown source.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Cover any cut or graze with a waterproof dressing and put on gloves before touching soil, sand, or gravel.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Work outdoors or over a large tray, cleaning spills immediately so no surface becomes slippery.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep hands away from the face throughout and wash them thoroughly before coming indoors.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if soil source is unknown or possibly contaminated.
  STOP: Stop outdoor work near any road, steep bank, or water body.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Return the soil, sand, and gravel outdoors. Pour all muddy runoff outdoors onto ground, or through a strainer into an outdoor drain - NEVER down a kitchen or bathroom sink, where it blocks the trap. The trays, cups, measuring container, and gloves are washed outdoors, stay out of the kitchen, and never return to food use.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Compare infiltration through sand, gravel, and packed soil in three cups on a tray indoors, or work entirely from a published watershed dataset. Kitchen materials or paper.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

science_brief: Science brief: groundwater occupies pore spaces and fractures in rock and sediment; it does not generally flow in open underground rivers.
Science brief: surface water and groundwater are connected: streams gain from or lose to groundwater depending on the water table.
Science brief: groundwater moves far more slowly than surface water, so contamination is slow to appear and slow to clear.
Science brief: extraction faster than recharge lowers the water table and can cause land subsidence and saltwater intrusion.

  SAFE ORDER 1. Use only the trays, cups, and measuring container labelled for this investigation. None of them has been used for food and none returns to food use.

  SAFE ORDER 4. Work outdoors or over a large tray, cleaning spills immediately so no surface becomes slippery.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Keep hands away from the face throughout and wash them thoroughly before coming indoors.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if soil source is unknown or possibly contaminated.
  STOP: Stop outdoor work near any road, steep bank, or water body.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.

  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.

Pour all muddy runoff outdoors onto ground, or through a strainer into an outdoor drain - NEVER down a kitchen or bathroom sink, where it blocks the trap. ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.
  ALWAYS: Never light, strike, or operate an open flame or a hob, burner, or pilot light for any investigation in this package; no lesson requires one.
  ALWAYS: Never cut, tear, puncture, or open a sealed commercial product - cold pack, hand warmer, glow stick, or smoke detector.
  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming carbon added to the atmosphere is removed on a timescale of a few years.
Claiming the fast biological cycle and the slow geological cycle operate at comparable rates.
Claiming ocean uptake of carbon dioxide has no chemical consequences for seawater.
fixed_facts: Burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from a long-term geological reservoir into the atmosphere far faster than natural processes return it.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Quantitative reservoir and flux figures, and carbonate chemistry calculations, are beyond this course.
relationships: Carbon moves between atmosphere, ocean, land biosphere, soils, and rock, on timescales ranging from years to millions of years.
The ocean has absorbed a large fraction of the carbon dioxide added by human activity, which has also made surface waters more acidic.
A carbon budget accounts for all sources and sinks; the atmospheric increase is the difference between what is added and what is taken up.

science_brief: Science brief: weather is the atmospheric state over hours to days; climate is the statistical description of weather over decades.
Science brief: climate is described by averages, ranges, and the frequency of extremes, over periods conventionally of thirty years or more.
Science brief: an individual weather event neither confirms nor refutes a claim about climate, though a change in the frequency of such events is climate evidence.
Science brief: climate predictability and weather predictability are different problems: the long-term statistics can be projected even where individual days cannot.

science_brief: Science brief: greenhouse gases are largely transparent to incoming sunlight and absorb outgoing infrared radiation, re-emitting some of it back toward the surface.
Science brief: the natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's surface far warmer than it would otherwise be and is necessary for life as it exists.
Science brief: water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide absorb infrared radiation because of how their molecules vibrate.
Science brief: adding greenhouse gases reduces outgoing infrared for a given surface temperature, so the surface warms until balance is restored.

disqualifying_errors: Claiming greenhouse gases work by trapping heat like the glass of a greenhouse, which warms mainly by suppressing convection.
Claiming greenhouse gases block incoming sunlight.
Confusing the natural greenhouse effect with the enhanced effect from added gases, or treating the natural effect as the problem.
fixed_facts: Greenhouse gases are largely transparent to incoming sunlight and absorb outgoing infrared radiation, re-emitting some of it back toward the surface.
The natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's surface far warmer than it would otherwise be and is necessary for life as it exists.

science_brief: Science brief: burning fossil fuels transfers carbon from a long-term geological reservoir into the atmosphere far faster than natural processes return it.
Science brief: carbon moves between atmosphere, ocean, land biosphere, soils, and rock, on timescales ranging from years to millions of years.
Science brief: the ocean has absorbed a large fraction of the carbon dioxide added by human activity, which has also made surface waters more acidic.
Science brief: a carbon budget accounts for all sources and sinks; the atmospheric increase is the difference between what is added and what is taken up.

safety_brief.h4_safety_segment_verbatim:
READ THIS BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANY MATERIAL.
HAZARD (physical): A lamp used as a light source gets hot and must stay away from water.
MITIGATION: Use an LED lamp only - never incandescent or halogen. Keep it at least 30 cm from containers, never above water, and let an adult position it. Allow it to cool before moving.
HAZARD (emotional): Climate content can produce genuine anxiety about the future.
MITIGATION: Pair every impact with documented response options and human agency, keep the framing on evidence and design, and let the learner pause or redirect at any time.
SUPERVISION: an adult must be within earshot and able to reach you. Do not start until they are.
SAFE ORDER - do these steps in this order and do not reorder them:
  SAFE ORDER 1. An adult positions the LED lamp first, at least 30 cm from the containers and never above them, with the cord away from any spill zone.
  SAFE ORDER 2. Fill and place the containers only once the lamp is fixed in position.
  SAFE ORDER 3. Record the starting temperatures, then start the timer.
  SAFE ORDER 4. Read from outside the containers without moving the lamp.
  SAFE ORDER 5. Switch the lamp off and let it cool before anything is moved.
STOP CONDITIONS - stop at once if any of these happens:
  STOP: Stop if any liquid approaches the lamp or its cord.
  STOP: Pause and move to the response-and-design strand if the content becomes distressing.
  STOP: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
  STOP: Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
  STOP: Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
  STOP: Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
  STOP: Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.
  STOP: Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
  STOP: If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
  STOP: A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
DISPOSAL: Once the lamp is off and cool, pour the water down the drain and dry the containers, then unplug the lamp and put it away. Nothing hazardous is produced.
ALTERNATIVE (equal credit, no special equipment): Run the energy-balance comparison in sunlight rather than under a lamp, or skip the physical model entirely and build the energy budget and carbon-cycle quantification from published flux data. Paper and calculator only.
ALWAYS - these rules hold in every lesson and nobody can switch them off:
  ALWAYS: Never mix household cleaning products; bleach combined with ammonia or acid releases toxic gas.
  ALWAYS: Never connect any investigation to mains electricity; low-voltage cells only.
  ALWAYS: Never fully seal a reacting, fermenting, oxidising, or warm mixture in any container.
  ALWAYS: Never have a flammable liquid open in the same room as a flame, hob, pilot light, heater, lamp, charger, or battery.
  ALWAYS: Never use alcohol, or any other fuel, for a flame demonstration; no open-flame demonstration is used anywhere in this package.

  ALWAYS: Never look at the sun directly or through any lens, filter, grating, or camera.
  ALWAYS: Never require a photograph, video, or voice recording as evidence of completion.
  ALWAYS: Never request or record a learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical history.
  ALWAYS: Never present invented measurements as real experimental results.

science_brief: Science brief: weather is the atmospheric state over hours to days; climate is the statistical description of weather over decades.
Science brief: climate is described by averages, ranges, and the frequency of extremes, over periods conventionally of thirty years or more.
Science brief: an individual weather event neither confirms nor refutes a claim about climate, though a change in the frequency of such events is climate evidence.
Science brief: climate predictability and weather predictability are different problems: the long-term statistics can be projected even where individual days cannot.

science_brief: Science brief: mineral, energy, water, and soil resources are distributed unevenly because of the specific geological and biological processes that concentrated them.
Science brief: ore deposits form where particular processes concentrated an element far above its average crustal abundance.
Science brief: fossil fuels formed where organic material accumulated, was buried, and was heated within a particular range of conditions.
Science brief: a resource is economically usable only where concentration, accessibility, and extraction cost permit, so the physical presence of an element is not sufficient.

science_brief: Science brief: earth's early atmosphere contained essentially no free oxygen; atmospheric oxygen accumulated from about 2.4 billion years ago, produced by photosynthesising organisms.
Science brief: oxygen-producing photosynthesis by cyanobacteria released oxygen that was first consumed by dissolved iron and other reduced material before accumulating in the atmosphere.
Science brief: banded iron formations in the rock record are evidence of that early oxygen being taken up by dissolved iron.
Science brief: the rise of oxygen transformed surface chemistry and made aerobic metabolism, and eventually complex life, possible.

The rise of oxygen transformed surface chemistry and made aerobic metabolism, and eventually complex life, possible.

science_brief: Science brief: mineral, energy, water, and soil resources are distributed unevenly because of the specific geological and biological processes that concentrated them.
Science brief: ore deposits form where particular processes concentrated an element far above its average crustal abundance.
Science brief: fossil fuels formed where organic material accumulated, was buried, and was heated within a particular range of conditions.
Science brief: a resource is economically usable only where concentration, accessibility, and extraction cost permit, so the physical presence of an element is not sufficient.

Science brief: hazard forecasting is generally probabilistic: the likelihood over a period can be estimated where the timing of a specific event cannot.

privacy: Records the learning target, completion state, evidence type, and next step only.
Stores no raw reflection text, no free-text answers, no photograph, no video, and no voice recording.
Requires no camera or video proof of any activity.
Collects no learner body measurement, health measurement, or medical information.
Requires no account creation, purchase, or disclosure of the family's location.
safety_brief.required_ppe: No protective equipment is required for this lesson's desk work.
sensitivity: Content is academic; no personal, family, health, or location disclosure is requested.
stop_conditions: Stop for any injury, burn, spill, fume, or allergic reaction and tell the supervising adult.
Stop if a material, tool, or step is not the one this lesson specifies.
Burn: cool it under running cool water for 20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or ointment.
Splash in an eye: rinse with running water for 15 minutes, holding the eyelid open, before anything else.
Fumes or a strong smell: leave the room, open a window from outside the room, and do not go back in to tidy up.

Fire: do not use water. Get everyone out, close the door, and call the emergency number. Smother a very small contained flame with a metal pan lid or a fire blanket only if that is safe to do without reaching over it.
If anyone may have swallowed a magnet, a battery, or any material from a lesson, treat it as an emergency and seek medical help at once. Do not wait for symptoms.
A pause, break, or switch to the alternative activity is never treated as failure.
safety_brief.supervision_plain_words: You may work on this on your own. An adult should know you are doing it.

disqualifying_errors: Presenting a recommendation with no acknowledgement of its uncertainties.
Treating uncertainty as grounds for taking no position at all.
Omitting the strongest objection to the proposed design.
scientific_correctness_authority.out_of_scope: Decision theory under uncertainty and formal risk management frameworks are beyond this course.
relationships: Defending a design means stating the evidence, the assumptions, the uncertainty, and what result would change the recommendation.
Uncertainty is a reason to state the range of outcomes and to build in adaptability, not a reason to withhold a recommendation.
The strongest objection is addressed directly rather than omitted.
